newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin lashes out at defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin lashes out at defence minister.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin lashed out at Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and the chief of the general staff on Thursday, accusing them of doing nothing to reform the army.

"You have done a bad job. I am not satisfied and must draw conclusions," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling the two at the start of a meeting of the Defence Council, which is expected to discuss military reform.
Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying Rodionov had done nothing to reform the armed forces since he was appointed in June, 1996.

"You have forgotten what the armed forces exist for," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying. He accused the minister of being unwilling to cut the number of soldiers and generals -- a key task of reforms which never got off the starting blocks.

Yeltsin promised during his re-election campaign a year ago to end conscription by 2000 and create a modern, professional army. But lack of funds and a marked lack of enthusiasm in the upper ranks have seen the deadline quietly shelved.

Rodionov is at odds with Yeltsin's top defence adviser, Yuri Baturin, over the reforms. The meeting of the Defence Council, attended by senior generals and held at the general staff headquarters, was expected to make a choice on the direction of reform. Personnel changes are also expected.
